title: A dead daemon's ports are free
goal: On Windows a dead daemon's host-contract ports stayed bound under its pid (CEO laptop: pid 28172 died on 2026-11-07, and 127.0.0.1:9090-9094 were still held a day later, so every later daemon fell back to the next block). Root cause, measured: std's TcpListener/UdpSocket::try_clone on Windows returns an inheritable socket handle although the original is not (standalone repro: original inherit=false, clone inherit=true). The daemon serves clones of all five contract sockets (gemi, gmcp, gmcp alias, A2A HTTP, A2A UDP), and every Command::spawn inherits handles, so every leaf service, probe and tool, and their children, held the five ports; the holders on the laptop are two hung 'ollama.exe --version' processes (pids 48168, 55760) that outlived the daemon and were never in its kill-on-close job. Each clone now has HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT cleared (UninheritableClone); elsewhere try_clone already duplicates close-on-exec. Live check on an isolated daemon (offset 800): no daemon handle is inheritable, and its leaf services hold none of the contract sockets (before: all five each).
acceptance: cargo test -p susi-daemon --lib a_dead_daemons_ports_are_free_while_its_child_lives --offline --locked passes: a stand-in daemon process binds a TCP listener and a UDP socket, serves clones of them as the daemon does, starts a long-lived child and exits; while that child still runs, both ports bind again. With a bare try_clone the same test fails with os error 10048 (address in use).
